verdict.rationale: Alloy's docs describe a publicly browsable API reference hosted on ReadMe, with 134 endpoint pages. It includes a 'Try It!' request panel and SDK snippets that execute against the sandbox or production bases, and a complete OpenAPI 3.0.0 document backs it. Together this covers both an explorable interactive reference and runnable examples. However, running requests needs the caller's own (customer-gated) keys, and the sandbox mode is a per-request dry-run over shared production data rather than an isolated environment. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the Try It panel, runnable examples usable without account credentials, and an isolated sandbox for safe experimentation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The ReadMe-hosted API reference (134 endpoint pages, publicly browsable) runs the "Try It!" request panel with SDK snippets enabled; execution uses the caller's own keys against the live sandbox/production bases.
Alloy serves its complete OpenAPI 3.0.0 document at the docs origin (servers sandbox.alloy.co/v1 and api.alloy.co/v1).
Sandbox makes no vendor calls, so you can test your integration without incurring additional charges
